summary.text: The introduction revisits action as Brahman's offering and then examines Arjuna's apparent choice between renunciation and karma-yoga. Through a long objection-and-reply commentary, the teacher distinguishes the non-knower's preparatory choices from establishment in the actionless self. Karma-yoga is preferable to difficult renunciation undertaken while agency remains; this comparison does not assign a further liberating task to an accomplished knower. Bodily activity can continue without personal ownership. Questions locate the listener's own eligibility and push beyond retaining a subtle ego as witness: the final standpoint is non-separateness, not an individual claiming either action or observation.

segments.heading: Chapter four prepares the new question

blocks.text: Duty is to be performed without attraction, aversion or ownership of results. The prior sacrificial series culminates in seeing all elements of activity through Brahman.
Arjuna hears praise of both renunciation and action-yoga and asks for a definite recommendation. The teacher treats the question as natural rather than dismissing it.

segments.heading: Why Arjuna thinks a choice is necessary

blocks.text: The commentary juxtaposes non-doership passages with the instruction to act. From Arjuna's standpoint, abandoning action and undertaking it seem incompatible, like standing still and moving.

An opponent objects that the prescriptions concern different qualified persons. The reply reconstructs Arjuna's assumption: both seem available to him as things to do, so asking which is better makes sense.

segments.heading: The knower is not another choosing agent

blocks.text: The proposed comparison is tested against the knower and non-knower. For the latter, preparatory options remain; for the former, the assumed agent underlying the choice has been corrected.
One who knows actionless self as his very self.
The knower is defined by identity with the unmodified, actionless self. Renunciation in this sense is abidance, not a fresh deed performed by a self-agent.

segments.heading: The commentary separates knowledge and agency

blocks.text: Right knowledge and the error of agency cannot remain coequal standpoints. An objection cites instructions to fight; the reply distinguishes audiences and the preparatory role of karma-yoga.

The accomplished knower has no further self-completing duty. Bodily maintenance may continue, but seeing and hearing are not owned as my deeds. The denial concerns agency-based practice, not physical disappearance.

segments.heading: Why karma-yoga is preferable for the seeker

blocks.text: The comparison concerns a non-knower whose sense of agency persists. Formal renunciation is difficult and partial when its inward foundation has not matured; karma-yoga offers a more practicable preparation.

The teacher returns to Arjuna's earlier question and announces that the opening verse's detailed treatment will follow. This session supplies the commentary's framework rather than completing that verse-analysis.

segments.heading: Eligibility is a question for the listener

blocks.text: A participant asks how the distinction guides one's actions. The teacher describes knowing definitions of Atma while still identifying as the body that sees, eats and breathes.
Where that identification remains, karma-yoga prepares the actionless recognition. Its role is not opposition to the final state but guidance toward it.

segments.heading: Even an owned witness-identity must be examined

blocks.text: A second question confirms the distinction of eligibility. The teacher says bodily roles can appear without constituting identity, whether householder, ruler or mendicant.
A subtle sense of mine may survive even when one observes bodily activity as witness. The final account relinquishes the separate owner of witnessing and recognizes every element as Brahman.
There is nothing other than Brahman

concepts.label: Brahmakarma samadhi
concepts.gloss: Activity understood as non-separate from Brahman.

concepts.label: Karma Yoga
concepts.gloss: Preparatory discipline for one still holding agency.

concepts.label: Sakshi
concepts.gloss: Witnessing used provisionally without retaining a separate owner.

concepts.label: mamatum
concepts.gloss: The lingering mine-sense that can appropriate body or witnessing.
